newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn budget gap seen 8-10 bln DM higher - source.
newsitem.headline: Bonn budget gap seen 8-10 bln DM higher - source.

text.p: Germany's federal deficit in 1997 will be eight to 10 billion marks higher than current budget planning, exceeding a constitutional limit that says the deficit cannot be more than government investment, a coalition source told Reuters on Thursday.

The new deficit plan, to be presented in a supplementary budget by Finance Minister Theo Waigel next week, will still be in line with the Maastricht guideline of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, the source said.
In 1998, the federal deficit will fall back below the level of government investment, in line with the constitutional requirement, the source said.

The constitution only allows the federal deficit to exceed government investment if this is to counter a "disturbance of the overall economic balance", which would be an embarrassing admission for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition since the economy is not in recession.
But the tax increases or more stringent spending cuts that would be needed to curb the deficit would hamper economic expansion, aggravating Germany's unemployment problem, the source said.

Waigel, who is straining to keep the 1997 budget in shape to qualify for European monetary union, will probably present the 1997 supplementary budget on Friday, when his 1998 budget is due to be presented to the cabinet for approval.

Current budget planning for 1997 foresees a deficit of about 53.3 billion marks, and the government has about three billion marks in spending it can carry forward from past budgets. Government investment in 1997 is seen at about 59.6 billion marks.
